name: TeamStarWolf - TeamPCP Supply-Chain Campaign of 2026 Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the case study of the 2026 TeamPCP supply-chain campaign: the Trivy release and GitHub Actions compromise (CVE-2026-33634), the Checkmarx, LiteLLM, Telnyx and Bitwarden CLI publishes and the European Commission cloud breach. CERT-EU names T1586.003, T1078.004, T1195.002 and T1005, and ATT&CK's G1056 procedures cover T1677; the other bindings are the study's own. Score 75: a vendor advisory, CVE record or government release describes the behavior. Score 50: third-party research describes it. Score 25: an inexact fit, or the February intrusion no source attributes to TeamPCP. Comments carry the study's source numbers.

techniques.comment: trivy-action and setup-trivy tags (19 Mar 2026); Checkmarx actions and Open VSX extensions (23 Mar); litellm (24 Mar); telnyx (27 Mar); Bitwarden CLI and the Checkmarx second wave (22 Apr); Checkmarx Jenkins plugin (9 May). Sources: [1] [5] [9] [11] [26].
Malicious Trivy v0.69.4 release across registries (19 Mar 2026); Docker Hub 0.69.5 and 0.69.6 (22 Mar); CERT-EU's mapping for the European Commission intrusion. Sources: [1] [28].

Release workflow redirected to an imposter commit (19 Mar 2026); ATT&CK's G1056 procedure names Trivy, KICS and LiteLLM. The hackerbot-claw pull_request_target abuse (about 28 Feb) is third-party research and unattributed. Sources: [1] [7] [18] [25].

Compromised credentials publish v0.69.4 (19 Mar 2026); separate Docker Hub credentials (22 Mar); the cx-plugins-releases service account (23 Mar, Wiz); PyPI credentials publish telnyx (27 Mar). Sources: [1] [10] [26].
AWS API key used against the European Commission's Europa hosting (19 to 24 Mar 2026), CERT-EU's mapping. Sources: [28].
AWS API key obtained through the Trivy compromise (19 Mar 2026), CERT-EU's mapping. Sources: [28].
A new access key created and attached to an existing user in the Commission's AWS account (March 2026). Sources: [28].
PyPI token exposed through the exploited Trivy dependency (litellm, 24 Mar 2026); GitHub and npm tokens harvested by the Bitwarden CLI payload (22 Apr, JFrog). Sources: [11] [14].
Stolen token publishes litellm (24 Mar 2026); stolen GitHub PATs run malicious workflows (Wiz). Sources: [11] [30].
Runner process memory read for secrets through the proc filesystem (19 Mar 2026); ATT&CK lists it for S9041. Sources: [1].
Runner filesystem swept for SSH, cloud, Kubernetes, Docker, .env and database credentials (19 Mar 2026); AI-tool and MCP configurations (22 Apr, JFrog). Sources: [1] [14].
SSH private keys collected (19 Mar 2026; 22 Apr, JFrog). Sources: [1] [14].
Harvest encrypted with AES-256-CBC and RSA-4096 before exfiltration (19 Mar 2026). Sources: [1].
Data taken from Checkmarx GitHub repositories (30 Mar 2026); mass git clones (Wiz). Sources: [9] [30].
CERT-EU's own mapping for the European Commission data theft (discovered 24 Mar 2026). Sources: [28].
Inexact fit: data taken from the cloud hosting Europa.eu (discovered 24 Mar 2026); CERT-EU maps the theft as T1005. Sources: [27] [28].
Exfiltration to a typosquat Aqua domain (19 Mar 2026), a Checkmarx look-alike domain (23 Mar) and a LiteLLM look-alike domain (24 Mar). Sources: [1] [8] [10] [11].
Fallback exfiltration to a tpcp-docs repository in the victim's GitHub account (19 Mar 2026); docs-tpcp (23 Mar, Wiz); GitHub fallback (22 Apr, JFrog). Sources: [1] [10] [14].
Typosquat and look-alike domains for Aqua, Checkmarx and LiteLLM (March 2026). Sources: [8] [10] [11].
Malicious builds staged on Docker Hub, PyPI, npm and Open VSX (March to May 2026). Sources: [1] [9] [11] [13].
Malicious source fetched at build time (19 Mar 2026); Bun runtime fetched by the Bitwarden CLI payload (22 Apr, JFrog). Sources: [1] [14].
Inexact fit: the ast-results and cx-dev-assist IDE extensions (23 Mar and 22 Apr 2026) served as a delivery route; ATT&CK files the technique under Persistence. Sources: [9].
npm preinstall hook in the Bitwarden CLI 2026.4.0 package (22 Apr 2026, JFrog). Sources: [14].
litellm persistence through a systemd service (24 Mar 2026, PyPA). Sources: [11].
The litellm systemd service is masqueraded (24 Mar 2026, PyPA). Sources: [11].
litellm persistence through a Kubernetes pod (24 Mar 2026, PyPA). Sources: [11].
AWS discovery within 24 hours of secret validation (Wiz); GKE scanning from exfiltration-linked infrastructure (late March 2026, Microsoft). Sources: [15] [30].
Malicious workflow logs deleted after stolen PATs ran them (Wiz). Sources: [30].
Inexact fit: ECS Exec use after the theft (Wiz). Sources: [30].
Trivy releases v0.27.0 to v0.69.1 deleted in the February hackerbot-claw intrusion (about 28 Feb 2026), which no source attributes to TeamPCP. Sources: [7] [25].
